title: Rollout bridgework notes and tight-window cadence - Nov 2027 (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for the 'bridgework' micro-rollout pattern: short tight windows (1-4 hours) where a small cross-cutting change must be deployed across hosted and dedicated routing layers simultaneously. Goal is zero customer-visible regressions and controlled short blast radius.

High-level plan (one-liner):
- Nightly prep + 2-hour daylight window on Tue/Thu this week, canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full over the window with manual hold-points.

Key constraints and assumptions:
- Change touches routing service + model-variant resolver (affects 3 regions: us-west1, eu-west1, ap-south1).
- Dedicated customers should remain on pinned variants; routing fallback must not redirect them.
- Telemetry retention for preflight captures last 24h samples; increase retention to 72h if metrics look marginal.

Owners & RACI:
- Release lead: Marcus Li (ops/coord)
- Runtime owner: Aisha Patel (serving-runtime)
- Routing & infra: Ethan Chen (platform-eng)
- QA / Canary signoff: Sofia Ramirez (applied-ml)
- SRE on-call: Rotation team (see oncall roster link in ticket)

Pre-window checklist (complete by -48h):
- [ ] Finish PR review and merge: serving-runtime PR #6123 (link above)
- [ ] Build and push canary image to staging registry with tag bridge-2027-11-08
- [ ] Smoke test matrix run (latency, mem, error-rate) against staging traffic pattern
- [ ] Update canary traffic rules and add observability tracing hooks
- [ ] Update RBAC keys and confirm KMS rotation not scheduled during window
- [ ] Notify CS + account owners for Dedicated customers with change summary

Canary window script (day of):
T0 = start of window
T0+00:00: Deploy canary to us-west1 (5% traffic)
T0+00:20: Observe 20 min: p95 latency, error spikes, token cost delta
T0+00:40: If green, promote to 10% and deploy to eu-west1 canary
T0+01:20: If green, extend to 50% via routing table update (ap-south1 stays at 10%)
T0+02:00: Final decision: full rollout or rollback. Keep a 30m cool-down before full switch.

Observability & gating signals (hard gates):
- Errors (5xx) > baseline + 0.5% absolute -> HOLD & rollback candidate
- P95 latency increase > 40% -> HOLD and investigate
- Token cost per request increase > 20% -> HOLD and engage runtime team
- Model-quality regression (eval set deviation) -> immediate rollback and postmortem

Rollback plan (pre-baked):
- Automated route rollback script: rollback-routes.sh (keeps previous routing snapshot)
- Hotfix image tags: bridge-2027-11-07 (previous good) available in registry
- Communication: Slack #release-ops and pager notify SRE if automatic rollback fails

Release notes draft (customer-facing bullets):
- Short summary: Small routing and model-resolution fix to reduce cold-starts and improve variant selection accuracy. Rolling out in a staged, monitored cadence.
- Impact: No expected API changes. Some requests may see lower cold-start latency and slightly different model variant selection in edge cases.
- Dedicated customers: No changes to pinned variants. If you observe unexpected behavior, contact success@redwood.ai or open RINF support ticket.

Post-rollout tasks (within 24h):
- [ ] Collect 24h telemetry and regenerate rollout health digest
- [ ] Run targeted evals on known corner-case prompt set
- [ ] Update runbook and capture any divergences in decisions
- [ ] Close JIRA RINF-8210 with rollout notes and decision logs

Open questions / notes to self:
- Should we pre-emptively bump KV cache TTL for 6h during window? risk: cache churn.
- Do we need an extra SRE shadow for ap-south1 given lower capacity? recommend yes.
- Confirm SLA masking for Dedicated customers if we trigger emergency rollback.

Quick links & references:
- Canary smoke playbook: confluence/release-bridgework-2027
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/6123
- Jira: RINF-8210

This doc is a working sketch — fill in timestamps, contact numbers, and attach final traffic-mod scripts before moving to in_review.
